utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, to everybody. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. A special afternoon to you, Mr. Stanisic, we are pleased to see that you are in the courtroom and that you will directly follow the proceedings now instead of through a video conference link. I was informed that you, Mr. Stanisic, would like to address the Chamber briefly on health matters, and I was also informed that the Simatovic Defence wanted to address the court in relation to the upcoming witness. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We indicated we would also like to address Your Honours concerning the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We've seen some correspondence in relation to that and will later see what is appropriate to be dealt with prior to the witness coming into court, and what would be appropriate to hear when the witness is giving his testimony. But let's first then -- it's on the record. Mr. Stanisic, the Chamber, and this is now put on the record, has received a letter. The Chamber has sought through your counsel whether the content of the letter could be shared with other persons relevant for this matter. We received an answer to that. Whether this is an appropriate way of communicating with the Chamber is still a matter in which the Chamber has not finally made up its mind. But if you want to address us on health matters you may do so, but there's no need to repeat what is already in your letter, and I can tell you that the Chamber is giving some follow-up to that letter at this moment. So, therefore, even though we might not here be convinced that this is appropriate way of communicating with the Chamber, we certainly did not ignore what you wrote to us. If there's anything in addition to what you've written that you would like to bring to our attention, you have an opportunity to do so now. THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, for giving me this opportunity to give you some additional explanations concerning my letter. [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not receive English translation on channel 4. THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] Is it -- can you hear me, Your Honour? I'm on -- the mike is on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can now hear you. THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] Okay. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please restart, Mr. Stanisic. THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, distinguished judges, I believe that you understand the reasons why I have addressed you in writing in connection with my treatment problems and, one could say, inadvertent but definitely negligent treatment which has led to acute thrombosis in my leg. You have, in my view, not been sufficiently informed of what has been happening to me. That is why I have sought your protection and your understanding, your appreciation of the state that I'm in. The -- there exists voluminous documentation of the military medical academy which is an elite institution in Serbia where I was treated for ten years as well as that of the Bronovo hospital and the Leiden University Clinic, they all show that this is the third time that I'm encountering serious problems with acute thrombosis of both legs. The doctors treating me here were aware of the fact that there existed the realistic danger of serious complications of this kind ensuing and that they have been and they are monitoring patients who have had serious forms of pouchitis or ulcerous colitis, and they were aware that because of the [indiscernible] of an organ in my abdomen, my colon, in a series of three of the most serious abdominal surgery operations, my organism has been producing complications in the kidneys for years, so that surgery had to be done in that respect several times too. They were aware that because of my protracted treatment with antibiotics, corticosteroids, and cytostatics I also contracted osteoporosis which is seriously endangering my spine. The problem with my spine has initially prevented me from attending the court sessions. In my letter, I have explained in detail everything that I had gone through in my cell during that period, living a life not dain [phoen] of man, because it was with great pain that I could at all reach the toilet, let alone do anything else. They knew that I had been treated for depression for several years back and that in the meantime, I was additionally encumbered by personal problems, all this led to a state in which I could not nor had the will to leave the floor on which my cell is in order to go out for some fresh air. They could not see that my life had become relatively unbearable. Although a number of physicians have been monitoring the state of my health, two of whom are specialist physicians whom you have appointed and who also visited me in Belgrade, and who are seeing me every five weeks here at Scheveningen as well as well as Bronovo hospital specialists and those from Utrecht and Amsterdam, none of them throughout this period of eight months gave instructions for the anticoagulation therapy condition to be checked. Because of their utmost negligence in that respect, I again have acute thrombosis, the etiology of which is unknown or is that but the damages are known. Even worse, I was returned from hospital to my cell and lived there for two weeks without any kind of medical supervision at all, simply they just administered a double dose of anticoagulation therapy to me. That's all. Nobody took a blood test to see how very fine my blood was in order to prevent any other serious complications from happening. Believe me it was a very difficult time for me. There was just this one nurse there who upon my insistence drew some blood for testing that is after a couple of days and at my insistence, and I don't know what the results of the tests are. Judges, there is something else I wish to impress upon you today. I had no doubt that you would take my letter into serious consideration, but what am I talking about right now? You are certainly not aware of the fact that endeavouring to inform you at any cost that my health condition has improved, in that endeavour, because of that, it is for nine months now that I have been for nine months now without a single -- the exception of a single day, I've been -- I'm being administered antibiotics, so which one? Mitrodyosol [phoen] is very hard on the organism. That is of course administered so as to counter my principal condition. Even a layman knows that even when the infections are of the most serious kind, one does not take antibiotics for a period of over six weeks. Also, without consulting my doctors who have been treating me for over ten years, corticosteroid therapy was introduced and is being administered to me although I received a treatment unsuccessfully for two and a half years in Belgrade and because of the contra-indications of which I had to recover for several years; namely, my physicians in Belgrade were not consulted about all these therapies. Nevertheless, I accepted the recommendation of Dr. Cazemier from the Bronovo hospital in order to be given a new biological medication, not wishing to obstruct the treatment or to create any doubt in my good intention to leave this courtroom, although he himself told me that there was no proof that this medication is efficient. I wonder, Your Honours, whether anyone can tell me what are the consequences that such treatment can produce? This treatment further involves in addition to all these, also strong anti-depressants, tranquillisers, analgesics, painkillers on a daily basis against the pain that I feel in the pouch and my kidneys and the spine. All this while it is in the realm of medical ethics and the medical profession can be considered and reviewed in a medical way, but, your delegated doctor Mr. Oldenburg [phoen] has warned recently that it is dangerous to take antibiotics for so many months and that further administration of antibiotics to me is impermissible. I'm not sure whether you have gotten this report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stanisic, I'm going to stop you here. You are entering into quite some details as far as your medical treatment is concerned. This Chamber is not blind nor deaf for what you wrote us, to some extent it's repetitious what you told us. Your counsel know exactly where to go primarily if there are concerns about the way in which you are treated because the medical care for persons detained in the United Nations Detention Unit is not primarily within the scope of responsibility of this Chamber. If it has an impact on the proceedings, then of course the Chamber will form its opinion about it. So, therefore, as I said before, we are giving some follow-up dealing with some of the matters. You are explaining to us because we cannot exclude that it may have an impact on these proceedings, but to further listen to all the complaints you have about the way which you are treated, giving us all kind of facts which of course we can't verify. Giving us opinions as to what should have been better done, that is not for the Chamber to do and I'm certain that counsel will assist you in addressing the right persons in asking for further or for a change in the medical care provided to you at this moment. Is there any matter with you would specifically address as far as we are concerned? THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] I really tried to put down on paper and to make an effort in order not to repeat things, but what is of the essence for me and something which I think you should know is that it is with trust that every week I sign a blank piece of paper which the physicians will use to inform you about my health condition. In an inexplicable way, this is publicly known. I don't know of any case of this having happened to any inmate in the Tribunal. What hit me the hardest is that in an inexplicable way, first it was put on the Tribunal site, that is how it was publicised, my talk with Dr. de Man your specialist, to whom I told the most delicate things about my condition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stanisic, that is a matter which is raised in your letter and on which the Chamber is seeking follow-up. So, therefore, it is about whether you are sufficiently informed by doctors and whether others are appropriately or inappropriately informed about these matters that is an issue which is part of the follow-up by this Chamber. So that doesn't need to be repeated. It was a matter which we took up. Any other matter? THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can only tell you this, just my view that you cannot just treat this kind of a disease, these diseases in passing, and that an objective picture of my health condition cannot be gained in this way. I respect this Tribunal and I wish to believe that I will be treated in a fair manner in this connection and that I will receive at least a single report on my health condition. Over the past nine months I have not received a single report about what is happening with me. The only information I get is from the newspapers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Just to briefly respond to that. There are many reports that the Chamber received and that were filed available to counsel, and they can communicate the content of those reports with you. So that is just a short answer to the availability of reports. Mr. Knoops and Mr. Jordash, I take it that you'll pay proper attention to communicating with your client the content of medical reports that are produced and are filed in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: We do, Your Honour. I think Mr. Stanisic is referring to the reports of the treating doctors which is also part of these submissions to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is another matter which, of course, is a matter of patient/doctor relationship and it's a matter which we have also briefly addressed in our follow-up. Yes, Mr. Stanisic. I'd like to conclude because you are addressing matters which we have, I wouldn't say resolved, but at least which we have included our follow-up on your letter. Any other matter which need to be addressed now to the Chamber which would be within the competence of the Chamber to say something about? THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stanisic. Needless to say that if you need a short break or if you have difficulties in following the proceedings, then, of course, you can always address us and that's, of course, a new situation since you are now in the courtroom which is slightly different from being at a distance. Then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Knoops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Just because we just observed that we didn't receive medical report for today's session. Can it be correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that there was a yesterday's report. I do not know whether the absence of the report, if it is absent, has to deal with the matter that Mr. Stanisic wanted to come to court. I mean, the main purpose of the daily reports were to be informed about his health condition where he considered that he could not attend court. It's not that if he attends court that we nevertheless would need to receive a daily report. I think it's mainly in view of where he claims to be unable to come to court. But we'll further discuss this matter. The situation has changed slightly. But I have not seen a report. And Mr. Stanisic has not raised anything which would be specifically applicable today which would cause us to immediately ask for such a report. Then Simatovic Defence want to address. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, on behalf of the Simatovic Defence I have a request to the Trial Chamber; namely, something that relates to the witness that is to appear today before this courtroom, and I will be very brief.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the number of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will be brief. The Trial Chamber is well aware of the situation and the circumstances that this team could not have any influence on. In December as soon as the Court went on winter recess, we started our preparations for the witnesses who are coming up, especially those who have -- who can be called the linkage witnesses. Witness F-005, that is to appear, we have tried to familiarise ourselves with his statement and to also find other documents that may be relevant to his testimony. Also, when once we familiarise ourselves with the contents of his testimony, we addressed the state organs with a request that they provide us with some evidence that might be relevant to his testimony and for our cross-examination. We are aware of the contents of his statement and we have submitted this request for cooperation. We've asked for a number of documents, but we've only been able to obtain a fraction of what we have requested, just a few documents that are relevant to his testimony, and many others that are relevant have not been resolved to this day. Also, when we familiarised ourselves with the content of his statement, we realised that it was also necessary to conduct an investigation and explore various circumstances that he mentions in his statement. We have attempted to get in touch with various individuals who might have some relevant information regarding the claims of -- that this witness puts forth. However, because of the time that we had at our disposal and also the circumstances surrounding all that, and I mean that this was a period of several holidays, all these circumstances actually made it practically impossible for us to accomplish anything, or at least not in a manner that would enable us to question this witness in an efficient manner. Also, and this has to do with the overall situation that this Defence team faces, we have, in view of all the thousands of pages that we have been shown, we have only been able to actually review some of those and we have also been unable to go through the documents, or rather, the disclosed documents, we weren't able to really go through them and find those documents that might be relevant and useful for the cross-examination of this witness. What we would like to request, Your Honour, is that we be allowed to postpone the cross-examination of this witness until such time when we can obtain the necessary documents and familiarise ourselves with the large batch of documents that we were provided by the Prosecution. We believed that we would be ready for that today; however, when we actually explored them and when we actually looked at all the things that we have been able to do, we realised that, in fact, we were and we are unable to cross-examine this witness in a proper way and efficiently, either today or at any time soon. So our request to the Trial Chamber would be to postpone the

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: prepare so that we can do our job properly and that is why we are here. And I know, of course, that our request is not a simple one, but I do plead with you because we are really unable to cross-examine this witness efficiently and properly at this time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, there's a request, would you like to respond immediately or would you like to do that later today?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Whichever pleases the court, Your Honour. I can give, I know in substance what the Prosecution's response is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or would it be better to first hear whether -- because the Stanisic Defence wanted to address the court as well to see whether you can give a consolidated response later.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Perhaps that is wiser, Your Honour. We can defer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honours, our application is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, before I give you an opportunity to address the Court, the Chamber has been informed about exchanges of discussions between the parties where -- certainly we are to some extent reluctant and hesitant to see what has been exchanged between the parties at earlier stages of the proceedings. We further have received the queries you had, at least the Stanisic Defence had on its mind in relation to quite a number of documents, and also some information which gave us the impression that specific elements in relation to this witness are linked to more broader issues which are the subject of pending motions, and the Chamber is not inclined to deal with those matters; that is, form of the indictment, challenge to the form of the indictment which was not initially raised within the normal time frame. We still have to consider whether good cause has been shown to raise the issue now, whether we still have to decide on matters raised if we would go to the substance of those matters. The Chamber is not inclined to hear a mixed-up version of this could not be used by the witness because we have received insufficient notice of that and that and that, where that is the subject of pending litigation, and I want you to be aware of that before you address the Court, that we are very much inclined to look at the matters without them being mixed up and that the procedural situation at this time is that we have an indictment, we have a pre-trial brief, and we have a pending motion on a challenge to the form of the indictment, et cetera, et cetera. So to introduce through the witness whether you have been sufficiently put on notice of A, B, C, D, and E is not the way this Chamber would like to deal with this matter. I just wanted to tell you this before I give you an opportunity to address the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The difficulty, Your Honour, with my application then is this, that it is an application to adjourn the cross-examination on the issue of notice, and specifically on the issue of notice relating to training and who it is the Prosecution say was trained, and who it was the Prosecution say were the Red Berets, and this application arises because of disclosure of yesterday in which certain new information was adduced and that information -- basically information concerning the group Mice, who this witness will now say were trained by the Serbian DB, and that new evidence and the lack of notice to the Defence is inextricably linked to a degree with the wider issues of notice concerning who was a Red Beret, who was trained by the DB. So I can address the issue of new evidence but with difficulty in terms of contextualising why it's problematic in terms of why we need time to investigate. But without touching upon the way in which the Prosecution's case, we submit, has developed in terms of the Red Berets and why this new evidence is so dangerous and why with need time is very difficult to do without reference to the indictment or the pre-trial brief. If Your Honour would simply allow me five minutes to contextualise why we want to adjourn in relation to the issues in the indictment and the pre-trial brief and the notice therein, then I can move very swiftly to the issue of what is particularly new but not exclusively new, as that is contained within the whole of the argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, were you referring to proofing notes when you said new information that came up yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. The proofing note which is ERN number 0350-1756.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that 14th of -- no, I've got only summary of additional information, 14th of January, but I have nothing --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This is the one, 14th of January. Sorry, it was disclosed to us on Friday I'm told. I beg your pardon. We have trouble getting it off the e-court and that was the problem, but it was disclosed on Friday last.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it was the -- okay. Now, if anything new -- first of all, the Chamber does not allow you to deal with the matters which are part of the pending litigation. As I said earlier, we do not want this to be mixed up. The indictment is there. At the time no challenged the form of the indictment was raised. It now has been. Whether we will hear that or not is still to be seen. We have the -- we do not want litigation to be taken from where it belongs and then to put in every place where it suits the party to raise the matter in a different context. So we are not allowing you to deal with that matter. We'll certainly deal with -- we'll seriously deal with the motions filed, first of all with the good cause as far as timing is concerned, and if then still relevant with the substance of it. As far as new information is concerned, it's not unknown that sometimes new information comes up during proofing sessions. If that new information is of such a kind that after we've heard the evidence that in respect of that new piece of information you need further time, then I cannot exclude for the possibility that we would allow you, on that specific subject, either to postpone or to recall the witness if further investigations have been done. That will be seen once we have heard the evidence of the witness and then also we'll decide whether such an opportunity will be given and whether that will be given in respect of the whole of the testimony or only on specific portions where you've indicated we need to check this or verify that. So, therefore, the -- any decision, and that's true for the application by Mr. Petrovic as well, any decision on postponement of cross-examination in its entirety or of the specific portions will be taken after the Chamber has further considered the arguments as Mr. Petrovic has already raised and which you, apart from the litigated issue, have an opportunity to briefly explain to the Court, and then we'll decide after the examination-in-chief whether any of the requests will be granted or not. So you have an opportunity now not to explain, again, the indictment, et cetera, but any specific issues in relation to your request to postponement of cross-examination, and again the Chamber will not decide before we've heard the evidence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will of course, abide by Your Honours' ruling. I will reference only this in relation to the indictment, one statement, and it will not be touching or certainly not repeating the arguments in the motion before you, but the evidence which is new which we seek to have with which basis our application to adjourn, is that contained in the proofing note I've just referred to dated the 14th of January 2010, and there are two particular statements which we are concerned with. The first is the first row of page ERN 0673-4825. And that's the statement at the bottom of the first paragraph there. "The name of the unit also changed frequently but the people were always the same." This is a witness, as Your Honours know, who suggests he was part of a unit, and in his original statement he referred to that unit as the JSN, known by civilians as the Red Beret. Your Honours will find the reference to that in his first statement in which he, the witness, notes that the Red Beret unit of which he was part, and this is the statement of 2004, and it's ERN page number 0350-1758, and the witness there states that the Red Beret unit he was part of was called the JSN and it had a particular insignia. The proofing note then changes the nature of that case significantly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I haven't found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: All right, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us the paragraph number?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That may assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Seven, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Of that page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The JSN special unit. And on Friday the proofing noted changed that and said no, that's not the case, the name of the unit also changed. And it changed frequently. Now, I reference the indictment at this point simply to highlight to Your Honours that the indictment refers to two units of Red Berets only and that's at page 4 -- sorry, paragraph 4 of the indictment wherein the special purpose unit of the MUP Serbia JATD and JSO are referenced as known as Red Berets. So first point I would make is this, that in his first statement the witness raises a wholly new unit, JSN, but I don't dwell on that for the moment in light of Your Honours' ruling. But what I do dwell on is this, that now, only three days before, we are told that the unit that the witness was part of was in fact known by several names and those names changed frequently. A fact we have not had the opportunity to investigate and we would like that opportunity. The second point is this, it's the -- on the second page of the proofing note, it's the -- of Friday, 0673-4826, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Second page. Let me just check that. I have to find that because I have a one-page document but perhaps they have copied only one side of it. Is it double?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's -- well, mine is two and a half sheets long, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that we are not talking about the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It begins with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It now appears on our screen. What the Chamber had was a document which states confidential date 14th of January, and the heading being summary of additional information. Now, it seems that you are talking about another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm talking about the document which is referred to in the one you've just mentioned. At paragraph 1, the witness made clarifications and they were recorded in a separate document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Has that been disclosed to the Chamber or sent to the Chamber? Mr. Hoffmann, wouldn't it have been appropriate to whatever is attached -- I've got -- and my staff tells me that this is the only thing we received.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, my understanding was that when we sent this material to the Defence that we did copy the legal officer. Right now, I can't exclude that we may have missed that. It was certainly our intention to copy the legal officer when providing these documents. At the same time, this document was uploaded into e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the Chamber has no access to e-court in general terms. I mean, as soon as it is released and if it is tendered then the Chamber looks at it unless it is otherwise provided to the Chamber. But let's then have a look at it on ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we did receive proofing notes for another witness, but not for this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it has been uploaded to e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. We have it now. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I see that the Court Officer has just uploaded it now on the screen, on the e-court screen for your review.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm still a bit lost, I must admit, because the references you have made to paragraph 7, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Paragraph 7 of the very first statement of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that's first few lines. Is that your -- what you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I was referring, yes, to the first two lines referring to JSN special purpose unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It says that upon completion of the training that he received camouflage uniforms and Red Berets with insignias and then he describes what insignias there were. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The description of -- let's -- one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber considers that we are better served by first hearing the evidence as the witness gives it today and to hear any clarifications or whether what we find in the proofing notes which is not in evidence which is not available to the Chamber is whether he actually means what he is saying there, and the Chamber is not inclined to start argument for three hours before we hear the first five minutes of evidence of the witness. That is our approach of the matter. Is there any other matter, Mr. Jordash, you would like to raise? I mean, questions as whether in paragraph 7 he describes a uniform he has been given or whether that was the permanent name under which he operated is perhaps a matter still to be explored. And once we hear what he says about this, if he says the names changed frequently, was he referring to how they were perceived by the population, is it the nicknames that changed, was it the name of the unit? I mean, all kind of questions which are better resolved by first of all focusing on the evidence the witness will give us. Any other matter at this moment, Mr. Jordash?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, there is one more piece of new evidence but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- I'm happy to deal with it as per Your Honours' indication at the end of the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if would you briefly indicate what it is, then perhaps during the break we can consider to what extent it is appropriately put as an circumstance which would oppose against even starting to hear the evidence of this witness or to invite the parties to cross-examine him on it. So, therefore, if you briefly indicate what it is, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This arises from the proofing note of Friday. It's on page 2 where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could we have that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's the comment at the top of the page on the left-hand column: "I want to add that the group of Milan Ninkovic, also known as Mice, was trained by Bozovic and his men sometime after the 3rd of May 1992." I would put our position simply like this: The indictment names two Red Beret units, the pre-trial brief does not name the Mice group as a Red Beret unit and neither does the opening, and neither did the witness in any of his statements until this statement on Friday. Now the Prosecution suggests the Mice group was trained at the Red Beret camp and therefore as a consequence were a Red Beret group, as I understand the Prosecution case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think what happens is that the Prosecution informs you about the fact that the witness raised this issue during proofing and whether the Prosecution has changed its mind on these matters, or whether in view of new information they want to seek leave to amend the indictment. I've got no idea how they procedurally want to deal with that, but I do understand that this is new information for you, and it might cause you to say that we need to further investigate that. And then on that specific issue, we'll certainly consider that as in relation to any other issue you would like to raise with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The other issues, Your Honours, thank you for the indication, Your Honours I can raise the other issues as they arise with the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I am -- the usual cause is to have sessions of 75 minutes, which would allow us another 15 minutes at this moment. Who is going to examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann is going to take the next witness, JF-005, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Protective measures in place being face distortion, voice distortion, and pseudonym JF-005 may be brought into the courtroom once it is confirmed that all the protective measures are well in place. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, may I take it that since there was some communication with the -- especially with the Stanisic Defence that you'll intelligently use that new knowledge and seek to avoid any unnecessary problems? If you know what the other party has as its problems, you sometimes can anticipate rather than seek further confrontation on those problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honours I'm not seeking confrontation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For example -- just to give an example, if there would be lengthy argument about whether or not a certain photograph is something the witness could say something about it, then you could argue that for ten minutes, you also could see whether there are any other ways of getting this photograph into evidence as a bar table document or as an agreed picture of a situation. I mean, there are many ways that lead to Rome or to whatever other place you'd like to go to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness JF-005. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear you. Is there any ... Yes, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There still seems to be a technical problem because the interpreters cannot hear the witness. If you -- if you have one moment, we have a technical problem.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness say something, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please say a few words so that we can test the system?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know, but I can follow everything that's being said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now the interpreters receive what you say. Witness JF-005, before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by madam usher, and I'd like to invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Witness JF-005, you will first be examined by Mr. Hoffmann, who is on your right, and Mr. Hoffmann is counsel for the Prosecution. You may proceed, Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, the court has ordered certain protective measures with respect to you and your evidence here today. These include the use of a pseudonym and face and voice distortion. Therefore, I will not refer you to you by name but instead by your pseudonym JF-005.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And I would ask that we first see 65 ter 5205 on the screen which is the pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not to be shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And, Witness, I ask you to look at the pseudonym sheet in front of you and direct your attention to where it says witness name, can you confirm that this is your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, this is my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And is that also your date of birth on this sheet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, this is the correct date of birth, as well as my first and last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And did you, in fact, sign this sheet yourself with your pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution tenders this pseudonym sheet into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar, that would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P136 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted as such under seal. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall giving a statement to investigators from this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I would ask that we please see 65 ter 5184 on the screen, not to be broadcast. It's ERN 0350-1756 to 0350-1768. This is a statement dated 24 and 25 January, 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, on the screen before you is a document purporting to be a statement given by you on 24 and 25 January, 2004. Do you recall giving a statement on these days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And if we can please go to the bottom of that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And if you would please look at the signature, if that's yours? That should be on the English original statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, that's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And if we can please go to page 12 of this document in the English version. There seems to be a problem in finding the last page of the statement with his signature. Given that he has confirmed that he has given a statement on the date and confirmed his signature on the -- oh, there we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Looking at this page, Mr. Witness, can you identify your signature on this page as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, it is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I would ask that we can see 65 ter 5185 on the screen. It's ERN 0672-5345 to 0672-5355. It's an additional ICTY witness statement taken in May 2008 and finalised on 3 and 4 November 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, on the screen before you, you see a document purporting to be a statement given by you in May 2008 and finalised in early November 2009. Do you recall giving a statement on these days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: I do recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And if we can please go to the bottom of the B/C/S original.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And I'll ask you if you recognise your own signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And finally, if we can go to the last page of the B/C/S document, that is page 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: With the same question, whether you recognise your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, that's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, did you have a chance to review both of these statements in a language that you understand before coming to testify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And did you have a chance to note some additional clarifications and corrections prior to your testimony in writing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, we did make some corrections and we provided explanations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I would ask that we now see 65 ter 5206 on the screen. It is ERN 0673-4825 to 0673-4827. It is a statement provided by this witness on 14 January 2010 in relation to the two prior statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, if you look at this document in front of you, does that table include all the corrections and clarifications you wanted to make to the 2004 and 2009 statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: I cannot see the entire text. I should see the whole text. Yes, that is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And if we can please go to page 3, that is the last of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is that document. That's the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, review this document in your own language and then sign it with your own pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And with these clarifications contained in this document, would you say that your two statements are accurate and true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, they are true, but they need to be supplemented somewhat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: If you were asked the same questions today as you were asked in 2004 and 2009 with those additions that we've just seen, would you give the same answers in court today here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point in time, the Prosecution would ask that both the 2004 and the 2009 statement of this witness are admitted into evidence, that is 65 ter 5184 and 5185. In light of protective measures ordered by this Chamber, we ask that the statements be placed under seal. The Prosecution has produced redacted versions of both of the statements that could be made public. Those are marked in e-court as 65 ter 5184.1 and respectively 5185.1. At the same time, the Prosecution tenders the additional statement of 14 January 2010 as it is part of his statement, which would be 65 ter 5206. The last document itself does not contain any details of the witness or any sensitive information, therefore there is no additional redacted version of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness JF-005, you earlier said that the -- you said they are true but they need to be supplemented somewhat. Did you refer to the additions and -- you had already made or are there any other matters in those statements which are not accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was referring to the already made ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then that being clear, any objections against submissions in evidence of the two statements and the -- I briefly call it the proofing note?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: In relation to the proofing note, the Defence do oppose the admission of that for the reasons that it contains the additional evidence relating to Mice which we would argue is new and should be excluded before that statement is exhibited. I won't, in light of Your Honours' ruling develop that argument unless Your Honours invite me to at this stage, but Your Honours have my point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Simatovic Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we subscribe to what has been said by Mr. Stanisic's Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will decide on the all three together after the break but since the body of evidence which is contained in the two statements is not in dispute, there's no reason not yet to start the examination of the witness on that. But since we need a break anyhow at this moment, it might be that the matter has been resolved before the examination -- the further examination even starts. We'll have a break and we'll resume at 5 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: The Chamber indicated before the break that it would decide about the admission --

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, you had indicated before the break that you would decide about the admission of the statements, the three, and I would ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both the 2004 and the 2009 statement, as well as the additional information sheet are admitted into evidence. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P137, P138 under seal, and Exhibit P139, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first two, let me just check now, the statements under seal and the additional information as a public document. Please, proceed, Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Part of the filed 92 motion were number of related or associated exhibits that are discussed in the 2009 statement which is now Exhibit P138, and I would ask that those be admitted into evidence before we continue with the examination-in-chief. We have prepared an updated table of that annex indicating which of those exhibits in the meantime have already been admitted so they need not be admitted again. I can maybe with the court usher's help hand over those but that would be just for ease of reference, if that assists the Court. And there are copies for the Defence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think there were specific objections also against photographs, is that -- and other attached documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: In the -- if I recall, in the initial response of the Stanisic Defence of the 92 ter application, there were, in fact, objections to one of the exhibits being 65 ter 5169, it's a collection of photographs, where in fact prior to the filing of their response three days before that in court with the agreement of both Defence teams, that exhibit was actually admitted into evidence. It's on page 4 of this updated annex. It's listed as item 13 in the annex to the 92 ter motion. This is already an Exhibit, P87. So I would think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that seems at least to be an answer to that. You are not seeking that we admit it anymore. Then on the other documents, shall we go through them one by one to see whether there are any. Number 1, photo of uniform badge worn. Any objections? No objections. Then number 3, Doboj payment list, 65 ter 4839. No objections. Number 5, payment list special unit in Doboj, 65 ter 5011. Any objections? 6 on the list is already in evidence. 7, 65 ter 3842, KDF file of Slobodan Katanic. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: There are objections to that exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me just find that. I beg your pardon, no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next one, 65 ter 4594, KDF application of Goran Djuric. No objections. Next one 65 ter 4485, KDF file of Makric [phoen], Mladen. I hear of no objections. Next one 65 ter 4574, KDF file of Todic, Miromir. No objections. Next one, 65 ter 4680, also a KDF file of a different person.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: There is an objection to this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The objection is, as I understand this witness's position, there's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, before you explain, can we deal with that in open session? Let me see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can we deal with it in further detail in open session or should we move into private?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think it's fine in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The objection is simple. It's an objection to authenticity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The witness himself has expressed doubt as to the authenticity of this document, and you'll find that, Your Honours, at page 0672-5345, which is the composite statement from the 2nd and 3rd of May, and the 4th of November, in which the witness at paragraph 35 states that he doubts the authenticity for two reasons. One, that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash is inaudible. Could he please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, you are invited to speak into the microphone so that the interpreters can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, I beg your pardon. The witness doubts the authenticity for two reasons: One, that it refers to the corridor being open between Doboj and Belgrade and at a time when it was not. And, secondarily, the exhibit mentions or purports to mention Mr. Frenki Simatovic, and the witness again notes that it's highly unlikely such an application would have mentioned him at that time, which is mid-May of 1992. In light of those reasonable, we submit, questions as to authenticity, we object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it seems to be more contesting the truth of the content rather than authenticity, which of course is not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But it's -- the content are unreliable and as such to -- and unreliable to such an extent that it suggests these documents -- this document isn't authentic. That's the way we would put our objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And any formal challenges to the authenticity, I mean appearance or? So apart from the content.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Apart from the content we would submit there's no indicia of authenticity. There's nothing which will indicate that it was authentic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you allow, may I just add something to what Mr. Jordash has already said and in full support of he has already said. This document, as far as I can understand, is a document that has to be filled out by the person applying for financial aid, so there is no way, nor has it ever been checked that someone has actually filled out this form in order to have some gain. When this was filled out and how, no one has ever checked that as far as I can understand the documents after reviewing them. And as Mr. Jordash has already said, and noticed, there are obvious problems with the document and the problems arise from the way that the document was created, and it was created by someone just putting forth some facts without this ever having been checked by anyone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think, as you indicated, there are separate issues. One is the authenticity and we have provided both Defence teams about the origin of those documents, of all those Captain Dragan Fund files. Those were handed over at the headquarter of the Captain Dragan Fund in Belgrade to investigators of the OTP so that's, I think, about the authenticity when they come from. The matters raised by the Defence, I think, are matters that are going to the weight to be attached to such documents, and I want to note that, yes, the witness makes some comments about that document but if you carefully look at what he says, he does question one of -- one part of the document, which is the certificate which is attached to it. My understanding of the procedure is that in fact persons who served in any unit could apply for funds. They would fill out the initial form, which is basically always the same in those files, and then that gets to the Captain Dragan Fund in Belgrade where they then attach some certificates or some decision-making notes. But again, I think those are matters that are going to the weight of this exhibit rather than the admissibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's move to the next one. This one is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow, Your Honours, just one additional note. The document by just looking at it we can see that there is nothing in it that actually confirms its authenticity. No one has ever checked that. There is no stamp on it. There is nothing showing its authenticity. We only see that it was filled out in handwriting and that is all that can be concluded from that paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have it briefly on our screen, the 65 ter 4680.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: If I may add, Your Honour, one thing. If we could look maybe at the last page in the B/C/S document, which I think is page 7, it does include also a passport copy of the applicant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber already indicates this, that 65 ter 4680 will be MFI'd, a number later to be assigned. I move on to number 12 on this list, which is 65 ter 44. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for interrupting, my client has just pointed out something in relation to this previous document. The particulars in the identity card differ from those entered in the form itself. Namely, the father's name is inconsistent. I just note it myself at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look at this to start with. The father's name being Jefto in the personal details, and you said that differs from?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 7 of the B/C/S, where we have the photostatic copy of the identity card, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just look at it. The word --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, the last name is different, it seems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem is I can't see what ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the first word, Your Honour, that has created this confusion. Namely, Lukavac actually obviously refers to the municipality, not to the surname. If that is so, I apologise and I withdraw my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because I see both Dusko as apparently the first name and Drobic as apparently the family name, father's name Jefto. So therefore it seems to refer to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, for the other reasons but not then for the last reason invoked, the Chamber will MFI that one. We had moved to 12, which is 65 ter 44. I didn't hear of any objections earlier, neither do I now. Next one is 65 ter 4479 -- Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I request that the witness take off his headphones, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's first establish whether he understand or speak any English. Do you speak any English, Witness JF-005, or do you understand English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Perhaps, I'll try to deal with it without reference to, if that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you can deal with it in the presence of the witness. Of course, I do not know what you are going to raise and therefore leave it in your hands at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The objection is this, that this Exhibit 4479, or proposed exhibit, is the result of a request from the Prosecution at the ICTY, a series of inquiries was made by the Prosecution of the Republika Srpska MUP and the report is purportedly in answer to those inquiries. The inquiries, Your Honours, will find at page 3, questions such as who were the members of the Red Beret, how was the unit formed, et cetera. And this document purports to be in answer to those specific questions. It is an either, we submit, an expert report, or it is a statement which ought to have been submitted pursuant to Rule 66 and the normal rules of disclosure, and it wasn't. And it is, in our submission, wrong to try to introduce such a report which is effectively an investigation at the behest of the Prosecution which, because it's introduced in this form, is almost impossible to challenge. We don't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, if I may cut you short. You are referring to Rule 66, it appears to me that the main problem might be in rules 92 bis, 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I meant to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's what you meant to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, therefore, you say this document was produced at the request of this Tribunal and for purposes of the proceedings before this Tribunal, and for that reason admission into evidence should be under rules 92 bis, 92 ter, or under Rule 89, but not through this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Precisely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think in the first place again on just a quick note on the authenticity, I think there is no issue because this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It has not been raised. Authenticity has not been raised, was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Ah, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, therefore, let's only respond to what was raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: On the issue on how and to tender this document, I would like to note and submit that previously, I think it was actually the last witness we heard before the break, the Defence itself introduced the document which is also on the Prosecution list, that was Exhibit D10, which was also an official document in response on some queries from this Tribunal to the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the matter of Debeli and others. It did also include matters of intelligence surveys or summaries, analysis as to the massacres at Djakina [phoen]. So from that point of view I would submit that we have already set a precedent even by the Defence. At the same time, we are happy to tender this from the bar table. We could also foresee that we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't it true that in view of the character of the objections, that tendering it from the bar table would even be worse because what Mr. Jordash actually is saying is that, this document contains all kind of results of what was explored and investigated, and that it's unfair to introduce such a document which was prepared for Tribunal purposes without having an opportunity to cross-examine the author of it. That seems to me to be the objection. And then to say, well, we can bar table it, is not a real solution to the problem is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I was about to add that in the final instance, of course the Prosecution could also call the person who signed this report, if the Prosecution would be allowed to call additional witnesses. That is obviously a possibility. But again, I want to note that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is blackmail, Mr. Hoffmann. Well, I say it with a smile. It's blackmail saying, well, of course we could call that witness, but then you would have to allow us to call additional witnesses instead of using the amount of time granted to you in the best way. You say, well, if you want more, then you should give us more time. That's not exactly, I'm saying don't take me too seriously when I say blackmail, but you understand what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. But I think it's certainly our case that we have taken note of the decision to limit the number of hours that we are allowed to, the number of witnesses, but that's exactly why we try to stay within those parameters and try to introduce some of the evidence through witnesses. If that is not possible, then at least we might at some point ask for through the respective motion for additional time. For the time being, I would not like to spend much more time on discussing this exhibit. If need be we'll just mark it for identification if the Chamber has still some doubts about whether or not this should be admitted this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, especially the argument on D10, Mr. Jordash, any response to that? D10 being a similar situation where the Defence considered it apparently not unfair, that's the argument raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Certainly. Well, the crux of our objection is one of unfairness. Unfairness arising from a lack of ability of being able to challenge. D10, nobody challenged it so of course no unfairness arise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would say if there's no wish to cross-examine why complain about not being able to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, it's, I think, a bit the same as with leading questions. A lot of leading questions are put to witnesses, and then to say if there's an objection against leading, well, but you have put leading questions to witnesses as well. It depends on whether there's any specific interest at any moment to use the option to object or not. Apparently here, Mr. Jordash does whereas you did not in relation to D10. Yes. This document will be MFI'd for the time being anyhow. I move on, 65 ter 5168.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Simatovic's Defence has an objection to the last three documents, but I would be happier if I could voice those objections without the presence of the witness. They are different objections to these three last documents, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that. I suggest that in order to avoid that the witness moves in and out, that I'll give you an opportunity prior to the next break and that is unless these three last documents that is 65 ter 5168, 65 ter 5015, and 65 ter 4493, could you -- I don't know to what extent you want to specifically deal with them, but could you postpone that until after the next break?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Registrar - you have an opportunity, Mr. Petrovic, to deal with the matter in the absence of the witness - I invite you to already assign provisionally numbers to the documents as we find them on the list, under number 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, although that one will be MFI'd under that number. 12, 14, with the note that 14 will be MFI'd as well. 15, 16, and 17, all three for the time being to be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the numbers are assigned as Exhibit P141 through P153. Exhibits P148, P150, P151, 152, and 153 will remain marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the others, that is, therefore, P141, P142, P143, P144, P145, P146, P147 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P148 marked for identification. P149 admitted into evidence. P150, P151, P152, and P153 marked for identification under those numbers. Please proceed, Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, in your evidence, you describe how you attended training at Mount Ozren with the Red Berets in spring 1992. Can you describe to the Court in a few words how you got recruited to the Red Berets at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: First of all, we did not know they were Red Berets, and we were recruited by the local political parties such as the SDS was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: At that time were you told who or which unit did provide the training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: We did not know at that time. We only later got this information after entering Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And could you tell the Court what you -- later on when you entered Doboj, around that time, what you learned about the unit and who provided the training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: During the training we did not know who was providing the training. When we entered Doboj, people were telling, and later we actually learned, that the course was being provided by the state security service. What we were only told at the time was that we were a special -- that they were a special unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Just for the record, if you refer to the state security service, of which country do you refer to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: At that time one could say that they were from Bosnia and Herzegovina, but as the people who were providing the training were from Serbia, one could say that they were from the Serbian state security service. In fact, I'm certain of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court who personally was in charge of the actual training on Mount Ozren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Radojica Bozovic was the founder. Riki, Vuk, and Njegos were the instructors.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court where Bozovic was from originally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: According to the information that we had, he hailed from Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Would you be able to indicate on a map where the camp on Mount Ozren was actually located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, I am able to show you where the training camp was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I would ask that we see Exhibit P80 on the screen. That is actually map 30 from the court binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, do you see Doboj in the middle of that map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And from there do you find the place you say the Red Berets had had a camp at in spring 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Could I ask the court usher, please, to assist the witness with a pen to mark the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, I would ask you to mark the location of the camp with a red cross and then sign the map at the bottom with your pseudonym and today's date, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this Exhibit P80 as marked by this witness indicating the location of the Red Beret camp on Mount Ozren in 1992 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? No objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P154, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P154 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And if I may just for the record, so that it's clear on the record, the witness put a red cross just north of the monastery on Mount Ozren close to Bosansko Petrovo Selo which is south-east of Doboj. I would then ask that we have the next exhibit, 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For one reason or the other the map is still on our screen although the marking has disappeared, I don't know whether this has any effect on -- has no fact on the evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: If I could then have 65 ter 31 which is now Exhibit P141 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, in your 2009 statement, Exhibit P138, at paragraph 6, you refer to a patch that was used by your unit in Doboj 1992. Is the patch that we see on the screen now the one that you were, in fact, using in Doboj at the times in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, it is one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Were there other patches or insignias at the time that you did use?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: No, this was the emblem that we used most of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: In your 2009 statement, and again that's P138, you refer to a visit of Franko Simatovic to the training camp at Mount Ozren. When you mention Frenki Simatovic in your statement, are you in fact referring to one of the accused in this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And apart from the one visit of Frenki that you witnessed yourself, were there other visits of Frenki Simatovic to Mount Ozren in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Not that I know of. There may have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Have you heard of any such visits?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have to raise an objection, but I really cannot do it in the presence of the witness, and it has do with notifying what the Defences here find out about what the witness statement will be. The entire procedure, the investigation, everything actually becomes irrelevant because things happen only once we enter this court. Actually, I have to elaborate on this to explain what I'm saying because there are some things that I hear for the first time and I have talked to him. On previous occasions, it is impossible that he hasn't been asked these questions before. If you will allow me, I wish to say a few words in this connection.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It is not "I have talked to him," but "he has been talked to on many previous occasions."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness JF-005, we have a few matters now which the parties would like to discuss in your absence. Although initially I had on my mind to do it just before the break, the list is growing. Therefore, could you please follow the usher so that we can hear what the parties want to bring to our attention. And would you remain on standby.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, let's deal with everything at the time. You wanted to make submissions in relation to the last three exhibits and now apparently in respect of the line of questioning. Could we first hear from you further details of the objections again 65 ter 5168, 5015, and 4493.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. As far as the first document is concerned, 5168, this document which has been tendered is a document where a number of vehicles are mentioned that have been stolen by some individuals. There are several vehicles mentioned there. I don't know exactly how many, three, four, or five, but in any case not a large number of them. In paragraph 40 of the statement, the witness, and I'm referring to the statement of 2009, the witness mentions 2.000 vehicles, Volkswagon Golf II vehicles. I cannot understand what the connection and I cannot in any way reconcile these vehicles to 2.000 vehicles and this document that is being mentioned here. I simply do not see that this is the way to actually tender this document into evidence. Perhaps there is another way that it can be done through this witness. Then further on he says that I believe that this document is authentic and that it is consistent with what I know about the events, but in paragraph 40 he mentions 2.000 vehicle, whereas in this vehicle [as interpreted] you can see that only a few vehicles are mentioned. So I cannot reconcile these two. I don't see that this is the way to do it, but of course, the Prosecution has other options and other ways through which he may tender this document into evidence if they feel that it is relevant and of probative value.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me be short. If someone says that 2.000 cars were taken, does that mean that they were all taken at the same time and dealt with in one report, or could it be that this report supports this testimony when giving at least one example of the report on stolen vehicles? And more important, is this a matter going to weight or is there any admissibility issue involved? Could you please start with the last one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I see it, this is not admissible through this witness, because the testimony of this witness about his own personal knowledge and what we see here are inconsistent. So it is -- perhaps I'm mistaken, but I feel that this is not the way to do it. They can either do it from the bar table or through some other witness, but not through this witness. That is the gist of my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where is the inconsistency?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I understood this correctly, they said that they had taken 2.000 Golf II vehicles. This is what is stated in paragraph 40 in the statement of 2009. Whereas in document 5168, totally different vehicles are referred to and there are only a few vehicles, just a few vehicles and not all of them being Golf vehicles, but different vehicles. I can't recall all of them right now. I remember there was mention made of a Mitsubishi or some other vehicles. I can't say for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have the document on our screen for a second, that is 65 ter 5168.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I would suggest that we go to the second page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's be very practical.
