First of all, I do not see an inconsistency if I say that 2.000 vehicles were stolen, that if we find a report in which it is reported that some vehicles including vehicles of that make were stolen, that that's inconsistent. It may be examples, and that's really a matter of evaluation and weight of the evidence rather than admissibility. Apart from that since you said, well, it can be tendered from the bar table, the objection seems to be an optical one. 65 ter 5015, Mr. Petrovic, what's the objection? And could we have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a document, you will see it in a moment, which to me it seems completely unclear as to the source of this document. Whether this is a telegram, who it is being sent to, when it was sent, and what points to its authenticity. So none of these things are clear to me. It would appear to have been retyped, and I have to say that I'm completely confused when I look at this document. I simply don't understand any of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I, sorry to interrupt, may I add my endorsement of that objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's yes, although, you didn't reserve your position at the time, but we have to decide on the objection anyhow, so therefore it's now a Stanisic objection as well. Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document was seized in Banja Luka in February 1998 at the Ministry of Interior of the RS, the Republika Srpska. As it stands these are two entries, log entries, of 3 July 1992 at the relevant time. They do mention Bozovic, they do mention his cooperation with the RS MUP, and when this was put to the witness, he made his comments that he made in the 2009 statement. How much weight at the end to be put to it is one question, but it's certainly, in our view, authentic. It's part of the witness evidence already in that that he makes comments on it, comments that we are not able to make because we are not familiar with the circumstances, but the witness was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take us exactly to that part of his statement. You said the 2009 statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: It's P13 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Paragraph 41.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Looking at another document it seems that both notes are in relation to the above-mentioned illegal removal of cars from the area, and it shows the cooperation between Bozovic and the RS MUP. That's all he says about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm not making a big point about this one document, but it flows from the previous document in that in our view, and I think we are now almost in the final arguments here, whether or not that will help the Prosecution case, but it does corroborate the witness evidence where he says that the Red Berets were in the area and that they were looting and that they were taking cars away from that area to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The problem is whether this could have been a document, you say it's part of a log. I've seen a lot of log-books in my life, but they usually are in some kind of a format. These apparently are two isolated entries in a log of which we have not even seen the title page. I don't know what the log is. Could the witness explain that, do you think?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I would not expect that he would be familiar with the actual log because he didn't put that log together or has not seen it, as is I my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then all his answers are not answers to the authenticity of this document, were they?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: No, on the authenticity, I refer to where the OTP got this document from. This information was provided to both Defence teams and it was my understanding from the latest e-mail exchange that on the authenticity of these documents there were no further issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: But maybe I misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, therefore, if you ask me to look at this document to say what is this, well, this is about 120 vehicle, I could answer a question as well, and it's relevant 3rd of July, so I would be a perfect witness for you, would I? I mean, let's try -- the witness says that -- apparently that vehicles were stolen. Now, you have provided us with a report in which theft of cars is reported. What we now see is a document, you say it comes from a log. A log of what? It has dates on it and says that a convoy of 120 vehicles has passed in your direction, and now the witness can tell us not knowing what the log is, not having ever seen it before, that this indicates or that this supports, it's difficult to understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: To cut it short, Your Honours, I will not insist on this particular document in the interest of time for the time being. If it be marked for identification, we may come back to it at some point, but I don't think that we have to spend more time on this, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it should have been given more thought in advance. Next one, Mr. Petrovic. 65 ter 4493. Perhaps we could have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this document was produced by actually printing it off of a website. The website's name is www.redberets.com. So as you will see in a moment, the contents of this document is in fact a picture, someone's picture of a snap-shot and history of this case as seen by an individual who then put it all in this document. Who was the father of the unit, who was the commander, who was not the commander, and so on and so forth. So in other words, this is a web site print out. I don't know who is behind this web site name, www.redberets.com and it's probably relevant, but what is especially important is that the witness says in paragraph 44 of his statement, his 2009 statement, he mentions there the name of an individual who knows something about this site. But what gives rise to concern according to me is that in his view, the history of the unit is truthfully and correctly presented on this web site page, but on the page we can see a whole series of -- a lot of information that has nothing to do with his statement. But by accepting the content of this website, he in a way supports the -- his own claims by saying that they are truthful and correct, that the history of the unit is truthfully and correctly and accurately presented in this site. So it is not from his own experience. And perhaps the author of this website could be called in as a witness, but not this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say you do not know who is behind this web site, the statement of the witness tells us that he knows. So therefore to say that you do not know -- of course we could examine him, and you could cross-examine him on the basis of his knowledge, whether he -- this was told to him by (redacted) but that's not an admissibility or an authenticity issue. Apparently, that's what the witness tells us, is that this was published on the internet and that he knows the person who published it and what his position was in relation to the Red Berets. All matters to be further explored, but not a matter which is affecting the authenticity. You may say that it should not be believed what this person says. That's a matter of weight and matter of evaluation of the evidence. But since the witness apparently has some knowledge about the person who is behind it, it seems that authenticity is not a primary issue here, but he can be examined on it. Any further comments in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my main concern is this, the entire history as perceived by someone else, he accepts claiming that it is true and accurate and that, in fact, is completely outside of his own knowledge and his own testimonies. We will see that there's also a lot of talk on this website about Croatia and other locations which are not part of his testimony. How can he claim that something is true and accurate if it is not -- if it is not something that is his knowledge, so that is all that I would have to say. I will not waste any more of your time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I just add a sentence or two in support and really all I would submit is that the exact phrasing of the statement is that the website is run by this particular gentleman. It appears as if the question reasonably must have been asked does this witness know who wrote that particular statement, and the question must have been answered that he did not. All he knew was that the website was run by a particular gentleman. So in my submission, it does go to authenticity, because the question and answer is staring us in the face that this witness doesn't know who is the author of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not to say that when further exploring the statement, the evidence of this witness that an authenticity might not arise. It's well possible that if he says, well -- if he says I was sitting next to him when he created the website, then the authenticity issue seems not to be prominently there. However, there may be other circumstances in which the matter may arise.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I suppose my objection is really that the Prosecution have failed to provide us with the material which would allow us to make a judgement. If they'd asked the question, then it should be in the statement. If they didn't ask the question, then we've in any event been denied the information. I won't press the point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Number 16 on the list, which is 65 ter 5015, is not admitted into evidence. And, Madam Registrar, the number given to it was?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P152, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is, therefore, now to be marked as not admitted. 65 ter 5168, 65 ter 4493, which had received I think P151 and P153 are admitted into evidence, and the rest remains as it was. Mr. Petrovic, you also wanted to object against the line of questioning, let me just find again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: In the meantime, if I may, Your Honour, there was one mentioning of the name of the person allegedly operating this website. I know that this witness asked us for the redacted version of his statement, that the name be redacted, and I would ask that we also redact the name from this proceedings --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's always better to first ask to go into private session before you make this kind of observations. Madam Registrar, the name was mentioned several times, could you make the appropriate redactions. Mr. Petrovic, the line of questioning was challenged, let me find it --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to try and explain this. My objection does not refer so much to the line of questioning of my learned colleague. It is -- has to do with how the Defence team has been informed and notified of what the substance of the examination of a witness will be. All these statements that have been exhibited today were taken in order to be used against these two accused, Mr. Stanisic and Mr. Simatovic. The first statement from 2004 -- the first assumption is that our colleagues, the Prosecution as conscientious and serious people, have asked this witness, have you, witness, seen Mr. Simatovic, that is only to be expected and I'm quite certain that my colleagues have asked this question also in 2004. In 2004 there is no reply to this question. The witness does mention Mr. Simatovic. He says that somebody mentioned him, referred to his name --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, if you are referring to statements, always give us the page and paragraph number so that we are able to follow exactly what your references are.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I will do that. Your Honour, the 2004 statement, paragraph 18.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down for the benefit of one and all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 2009 paragraph 12, after five years in other words --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in the 2009 statement, paragraph 12, five years later this story appears. It says, I saw him personally once and that he came to the camp on Mount Ozren. That is in paragraph 12. He was interviewed in 2004, 2008, 2009, 2010, a couple of days ago, in fact, and today the witness said that he had heard about some other visits as well. That is page 44 and 45 today. And to a quite leading question in fact. He knew of this one visit and then today he said yes, I did hear something, meaning about some other visits as well. As we are in a difficult situation as it is, but how can we proceed under these circumstances when first from a state of there have been no visits by Simatovic, now we have come to a state of multiple visits by Simatovic. So we have not been notify of what the testimony will be. I'm quite certain that colleague Hoffmann has asked him about this and has put down, has jotted down what he asked him about today, and these things are actually putting us in this state of quandary now. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, Mr. Petrovic -- Mr. Hoffmann, to try to make matters simple, what actually Mr. Petrovic is saying is that the statements are to some extent inconsistent, and that when you put questions to the witness that the inconsistency even grows because there comes more. Now, apart from whether this would not give a brilliant opportunity to Mr. Petrovic for cross-examination, of course the first question is whether you would disagree that there is some inconsistency and that it may be a bit difficult if the statements would be inconsistent in a certain respect, that you could have them admitted both under Rule 92 ter that is attested as to the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I try to be very brief. In the first instance, in the 2004 statement, that is Exhibit P137 at paragraph 18, it did read: "Rajo Bozovic told us that the chief would come, and I suppose it was Frenki Simatovic who was the commander of the special units of the Serb NDP." Now, obviously this is not particularly clear which is why when I met the witness I did ask him about it. The initial meeting we had was in 2008. A draft statement was taken because of the timing and that was all explained in the various litigations on the issue of when and how to add this witness to the witness list. I have taken a draft statement and submitted that to the Defence teams in 2008 as a matter of notice, although the witness at the time did not have a chance to review it. In this draft 2008 statement, just as in the final 2009 statement which is now Exhibit P138, he especially refers to paragraph 18 of the old statement and then clarifies that he had seen him once. And, in fact, to add that in the 2008 draft statement, it also included the sentence that he did hear of other visits of Frenki Simatovic to Mount Ozren. Due to an interpretation mistake, this one sentence was left out when it was translated into B/C/S which was then used during the final interview. In any event, the Defence since the early days had notice of it and since 2008 had notice that he also talked about that he heard about other visits. For me, it's clearly a matter of cross-examination I really wonder how much more time you want to spend on possible ways of cross-examination rather than to expect them to do their job during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, there's no need to assist me in conducting this trial and giving suggestions as to what I should say to the other parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The explanation given leads the Chamber to decide that the objection against -- well, it's not clear against what exactly the line of questioning or the way in which the Prosecution proceeds is denied. We will have a break, but before doing so --

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hoffmann?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Just one procedural matter, if I may, quickly raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: It wasn't clear to me if, for the statements, already the redacted versions were already admitted as well or if that is to be decided later, but?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I -- again, I must say after quite a long recess, I have to check again with the Registrar how we dealt with the redacted statements, whether they were just to be filed or whether they had to be admitted into evidence. Just it's not clear on my mind anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may just add because Mr. Hoffmann isn't aware of this, but the press people downstairs have made a complaint to our press office saying they are finding it impossible to follow what's happening today without a redacted copy of the statement, so it's really conveying their request and their frustration at being at a loss as to what's happening. So if the Chamber were able to decide over the break about whether redacted versions could be tendered, I think they would greatly appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and my concern is that we have the same evidence twice there, one apparently not for the purposes of this proceedings but for the outside world, and I wonder whether there are any other ways to resolve that problem. I'll further briefly discuss the matter. There is -- there may be other ways of achieving the same goal. I also would like to urge the parties to be -- to show some self-restraint in objections. For example, to say that the names are different, then we look at it and they turn out not to be different, I think that this should have been verified by that counsel before raising the matter. The argument in relation to procedural matters, and I give another example, having long arguments on a document and then to say well, we would not oppose against admission as a bar table document, of course could have been shortened quite a bit by saying, although we find it inappropriate that this is introduced through this witness, we nevertheless do not object against admission, although a bar table submission would have to be preferred. That's three lines instead of two pages. The Chamber is primarily focusing on hearing evidence in this case and seeks a fair balance between procedural matters necessarily and appropriately be raised and spending its time on hearing the evidence. We will have a break and we'll resume at 5 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, if I may refer you to your 2009 statement which is Exhibit P138. In paragraph 31 you stated that in May 1997 you have been present at a ceremony in Kula in Serbia. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you explain the Chamber what the Kula camp was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: It -- it wasn't a camp, it was sort of a command of the special operations unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you give us the official title of the unit at the time in May 1997?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: The special operations unit, or the unit for special operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And the correct abbreviation for that would be JSO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And to what organ or official body, if any, did this unit belong to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: It belonged to the state security department, the state security as we referred to it. The state security service, as we referred to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will now play a couple of clips from a video that has previously been admitted as Prosecution Exhibit P61. I want to note just for the clarity that we can see on the clips that we will play a time code that is actually on the screen which at times differs about 1 second from the time code that is seen on the Sanctioned file. Whenever I do refer to the time codes in the next questions, I do refer to the time code as it is shown on the video itself, in white font.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the transcript been provided to the booth?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: We did provide the transcripts to the booth. I see them nodding. We have marked the individual clips by numbers, and we will start the first clip at 1 minute 14 and stop again at 1.20.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "How are you? "Good, am I one of them? "Certainly not one of the veterans, excuse me, veterans."

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise either of the two men that we can see in this frame at 1 minute 20?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: I do, I recognise the first person.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court who that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: The first person is Radojica Bozovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Again, just for the record, you refer to the right person on this shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: The first person on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Is that the same Rajo Bozovic whom you mention in your statement as being the leader of the Red Beret unit you served in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: We will continue until 1 minute 25 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, again there are two men in this shot, one with glasses, do you recognise either of these men in the frame at 1 minute 25?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Dragan Opacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Which one of the two is he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: The one on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: We will then play a second clip which starts at 5 minutes 50 of the original tape and pause again at 6 minutes 36.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Mr. President: Special operations unit of the state security service of the Republic of Serbia is ready for inspection. Unit commander Colonel Milorad Lukovic reporting. "Hello Lukovic."

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, you see three persons in this shot at 6 minutes 36. Do you recognise the three men on this screen shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. Interpreter's correction: "Yes, I do."

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell the names of the three persons starting from the left side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: The first person on the left is Jovica Stanisic. Next to him is Slobodan Milosevic, and behind them you can see Milorad Ulemek.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: We then play a third clip, we continue at 12 minutes of the original tape and pause again at 12 minutes 20 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Go ahead. "Mr. President, allow me to -- how it -- where it originated and what it means now ... at ease."

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, just for the record, you see one person on this screen at 12 minutes 20 seconds, who is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we will play now a longer clip which runs until 19 minutes 29. It shows the accused, Franko Simatovic, giving a speech in Kula. Once this has been played, I will address certain questions with this witness. This is still part of what is marked for the booth as clip 3.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Mr. President, we thank you for accepting the invitation to attend the ceremony marking the anniversary of the formation of the special operations unit of the state security service. It was constituted on the 4th of May, 1991, at the time of the break-up of the former Yugoslavia and since it emerged has constantly worked to protect national security in circumstances where the existence of the Serbian people was directly jeopardised throughout its entire ethnic area. Its combat operations were anti-terrorist, directed at preventing war crimes, mass retaliation, and genocide. "From the first moment of its existence and establishment, the unit has passed through a heroic epic, and its path has been one of the most difficult ones in the history of the struggle. Due to the international circumstances familiar to us all, we were forced to operate in a complete secrecy. And despite wartime conditions: Fighting with Croatian and Muslim troops, the presence of numerous United Nations international forces - later IFOR and SFOR - and numerous instruments of foreign intelligence services in the field where the unit is not. The contribution of the special operations unit is enormous. Forty-seven soldiers were killed and 250 wounded in combat operations at 50 different locations. "We are proud of the unit's level of professional training, which meets the highest international standards, and the unit has never experienced defeat. One of its most recent successes was its engagement in the freeing of 400 UNPROFOR hostages in Republika Srpska, which met with a very positive response in the international community and made our country's position stronger. One of the units's most successful actions in our territory was the capturing of the national guard corps terrorist group caught in the Apatin area in 1993. "Mr. President, allow us to inform you briefly about the unit's history, its combat record, present situation, and function. When it was formed, its core was made up of members of our service, Republic of Serbian Krajina police, and volunteers from Serbia. The second war service intelligence administration, which was also set up at the time, included a special team for offensive and logistical support of the special operations unit. "From the 12 October 1991, in battles with armed Croatian police forces in the zones of Benkovac, Stari Gospic, Plitvice, Glina, Kostajnica, and others, the unit provided important support in the liberation of all areas of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. Around 5.000 soldiers were engaged in these battles and their actions were co-ordinated by the unit command and an intelligence team from the second administration. "In May 1991, an air helicopter squadron was formed which transported tonnes of special shipments, equipment, troops, and machinery from the improvised airfields of Medeno Polje, Petrovac, Velika Popina, SRB, and Udbina, and carried out numerous complex tasks while war operations were ongoing. "In September 1991, a part of the unit was transferred to Serbia, where it's reconstruction was conducted and high quality professional training organised. These two units were involved in operations in Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. Twenty-six training camps were for Special Police units of Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina were also formed in that period. In the Republic of Serbian Krajina in Golubic, Dinara, Obrovac, Gracac, Plitvice, Sumarice, Petrova Gora, Licki Osik, Benkovac, Lezimir, Ilok, and Vukovar and in RSK in Banja Luka, Doboj, Samac, Brcko, Bijeljina, Trebinje, Visegrad, Ozren, and Mrkonjic Grad. "Units of Serbian were involved in six large joint operations in Eastern Slavonia, the corridor at Brcko in the Drina, Sarajevo, and Maglaj operations. In Western Bosnia, the unit was the backbone of Fikret Abdic's army with around 15.000 soldiers who freed most of Cazin Krajina. "Also in 1992, they began building and securing a network of small air fields in Bosnia-Herzegovina and also forming a combat squadron. Around a thousand combat, reconnaissance, transport, and humanitarian flights were made from the airfields in Bratunac, Skelani, Sokolac, Rogatica and others. In mid-spring of last year, it retreated from these parts with complete equipment and machinery, helicopters, and aircraft. Throughout that period, its operation remained undetected, despite NATO's sophisticated equipment and intensive investigation by a number of foreign intelligence services. The unit's humanitarian activities throughout the entire period are also substantial. "One of them was the promotion of Captain Dragan's Fund, which employs 150 wounded persons and cares for over 2.500 children of soldiers killed, and also mediates in the employment of around 6.000 socially deprived persons, for the most part. After the end of war, in the area of the former Yugoslavia, the special operations unit was demobilised and its numerical strength was, of course, adapted to present conditions and obligations. With a new organisation, which began effective in the service as of May of last 36 years, the unit was reduced to 593 members which operates at 75 per cent of strength. The current reserve force is of company strength, made up of former soldiers who are trained to maintain a constantly high level of combat readiness. Part of the special operations unit organisation are units to battalions, companies, and platoons, and also a helicopter squadron. In addition, tactical services providing logistical, medical, intelligence, and counter-intelligence support are also part of the unit. "The centre in which we are now bears the name of Radoslav Kostic, a distinguished member of this unit who was killed three years ago in Western -- the service took over this building in February 1995 in a very damaged condition, and prior to that, from 1999, it had served as a refugee reception centre. "You will have the opportunity to see that we have managed to build a modern centre with training grounds, a firing range, a heliport, dispensary, hangars, and other facilities. Due to functional needs, we have planned the construction of a number of tactical facilities, and some of them have already been put into operation. "Mr. President, the special operations unit is in the stage of being trained for operations against terrorism and other forms of jeopardising the country's security. It represents an important contribution to the elimination of all potential threats to the national and state security of Serbia, which is mobile and professionally capable of acting quickly and efficiently in any part of the country or abroad. Thank you. "Would you like to have a look?"

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, Frenki Simatovic has given the date of the founding of the unit as 4 May 1991. Do you have any comment on that particular date given by the accused Frenki Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: According to what I know, I believe that at that time the camps began to be established and the training started, but what other members told me in casual conversation was that it had been established much earlier, perhaps that was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: In his speech, and that would be at page 9 of the English transcript, we can find the following quote from the accused Frenki Simatovic: "And since it emerged has constantly worked to protect national security in circumstances where the existence of the Serbian people was directly jeopardised throughout its entire ethnic area." Witness, what does that term mean to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: To me, it means that in a city or in a region where there are the Serbian people or where there is a Serbian majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Do you understand the accused referring to areas within the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: No, no, actually he was referring to places outside the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you be more precise in what you understand these areas would be that he referred to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: For instance, the Knin Krajina, Banja Luka, to be more specific Doboj where there is a Serbian majority, in municipalities where there was a Serbian majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: The accused Simatovic has listed a number of locations, and that is to be found on page 10 of the English transcript, like Benkovac, Stari Gospic, Plitvice, Glina, Kostajnica, where he claims that the unit had battles with Croatian forces from 12th October 1991 onwards. Could you tell the Court where these areas are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: These locations are in the area of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Did you ever hear from any of your colleagues in the Red Berets or the JSO about actions they had participated in this region?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry to, maybe I've missed the disclosure, but I don't know if this has been disclosed, this aspect of the witness's evidence? I didn't appreciate he was going to go into issues relating to these various areas. Maybe I've missed something in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, could you -- apparently Mr. Jordash misses the link between what he expected to be the testimony on the basis of these statements. Could you help him out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. For instance in the 2009 statement at paragraph 17 it does refer to the witness talking to Bozovic and the other instructors, Vuk and Riki, about their experience and their first training in Golubic in 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- Mr. Jordash, Golubic is, from what I know, is in the Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour, and it's the question was asked about actions in particular locations. What my learned friend has just referred to is evidence relating to training at Golubic. What my learned friend is asking about, it would appear, is military operations of this so-called special unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: It is clearly the Prosecution's understanding that not every piece of the expected testimony has it to be disclosed line by line. This clearly falls into the general evidence that has been disclosed previously. We have this part of Frenki Simatovic speech already in evidence, and I'm just questioning this witness about his knowledge about it without going in any further detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll see how it further develops and see whether it goes into such detail as it would have been unfair for the Stanisic Defence not to be aware of the type of questions you are putting to the witness. So you may proceed, but this is not a green light forever.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, may I just repeat my question. Did you ever hear from your colleagues in the Red Berets, and/or the JSO, about actions they had participated in this region that we just heard about from Frenki Simatovic and the RSK?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, there was talk about it, but I have no information about specific actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And is what Mr. Simatovic in his speech says about the -- generally about the actions in the Croatian Krajina consistent --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry to object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Shall we first listen to what the question is before we object. Please do not answer the question yet, Witness. Yes, continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, I was just about to ask you whether what you heard from your colleagues if that is consistent with what Mr. Frenki Simatovic says in his speech about the actions in the Croatian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The objection stands, Your Honour. At the heart of the Prosecution case is this alleged unit and its crimes committed in these locations, and my learned friend is seeking to elicit the core of the case which he clearly has discussed with the witness previous and has failed to disclose it to the Defence but is seeking to just take advantage by eliciting it in open court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point in time --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just to supplement very briefly. A few rows above, the witness said there was talk about it but I have no information about specific actions. I believe that puts an end to that particular line of questioning. That that is all that Mr. Hoffmann can elicit from this witness on that score. Anything else would be leading him on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily, but Mr. Hoffmann, it's clear that the witness says the only thing I heard a bit -- we have seen on the video and heard on the video what Mr. Simatovic was claiming. In what direction are you going? If you say, well, this witness would confirm that others were talking about that, well, then, it gives some support, but I would say the real weight of what was said is found in the video rather than by a witness who says that he heard other peoples talking about it. So, therefore, I'm wondering what the purpose is to seek rather general and weak support for something which seems to be at least at first sight to be a very focussed explanation of what the unit had done.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the content of this video and the speech of one of the accused in this case seems to be a matter of contention, especially interpretation of that speech. That is why I am exactly going down the road that you have just indicated. We have a witness who was a member of the unit, who talked to colleagues of the unit, and we have general comments of the accused, and he can confirm those --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we've heard from the witness now that he heard others talk about it without any further specifics. That's where we are. What else is there? I mean, put a question and there was an objection to leading in this respect, put your next question to the witness and see what it brings; although, I wouldn't say that it's the expectations expressed by Mr. Petrovic are without any merit. So please proceed, but let's be very precise in our questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, if I just repeat my question. You have just said that you talked to some of your colleagues in the units about the events in Croatia. You have heard what Frenki Simatovic said about -- generally about the actions in the Croatian Krajina. Does what you heard from other unit members match to what you heard from Frenki Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have really to know whether it matches or not. If I say the summer of 1998 was a brilliant summer, and if in another statement it says the weather was good at the beach, all kind of details, and then to say to match it, doesn't give us any further information. If you are seeking matching points, you should ask the witness exactly at what points what he heard from his colleagues was matching with what he saw on this video. Could you please answer that question. You said you didn't receive any further details. I think you said -- now, what you heard here, is there anything in this which was told to you by your colleagues as well, and if so, what details there were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, one can conclude from this speech that it does actually correspond to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You are not invited to draw conclusions from the speech. What did they tell you? You earlier said that without giving any details this is what they -- some of it was told to you. Now, what did they tell you exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, for instance, they told me where the first camp had been established, how the training went on, how they grew, and new camps were being established, how the Republic of the Serbian Krajina was being defended and so on. That they were defending the interests of the Serbian people in Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also the place names. They mentioned the places where these camps were, but a lot of time has passed in the meantime and I can't recall them all. It's been 17 years or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, you just mentioned the camps that Frenki Simatovic talks about. Are you personally familiar with any of the mentioned training camps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Well, they said that the system was the same as at the Ozren camp, that they were established in the same manner and that the training that was conducted there was the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Do you understand the reference to Mount Ozren being the same place that you were trained at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, is my recollection right that there was no reference to Mount Ozren, but to Ozren?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, then you are adding something. I mean, to say is the reference to Mount Ozren the same as what was earlier considered to be Mount Ozren, if the only thing which was said was Ozren, of course you answer the question yourself and of course the witness is supposed to give evidence and not you, and I and invite you to be very precise on these matters. One additional question, Witness JF-005, you said: "Well, they said that the system was the same as at the Ozren camp." Who is "they"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The people who were our instructors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Frenki Simatovic also mentioned a camp location at Golubic in the Republic of Serbian Krajina. Is that the same or another place as you mentioned in your 2009 statement at paragraph 4 where Bozovic, Vuk, and Riki had been trained in 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Correction, they were trained. That's -- that is the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge of any other of the camp location that were mentioned besides from the one in Doboj and Ozren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: There was a camp in Banja Luka, in Samac, in Brcko, there was a small camp in Teslic. Yes, there were some other camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Have you seen those camps personally or did you hear about them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Well, I did see the Banja Luka camp myself, but as for the others, I had heard about them, but there is no reason for me to suspect or not to believe that they existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Further on, Mr. Simatovic has referred to, and I quote, "new organisation" of the unit. Are you familiar with this term or this new organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Well, probably he just referred to the re-organisation within the unit itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry to interrupt, Mr. Stanisic requests leave to use the mens' room but he has no objection if we continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then leave is granted, and if he has no objection, we'll also continue. Mr. Hoffmann, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Frenki Simatovic has mentioned a special operation unit intelligence and counter-intelligence support. Do you personally know anything about the way in which the unit's intelligence and counter-intelligence support functioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: I personally was not involved in that and I do not know how it functioned. I know what I was told by others, but as for the inner workings of the intelligence or counter-intelligence service, I really don't know about that anything, and I wasn't there. I wasn't present myself.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure of the last words that the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your last words because the interpreters were not sure that they caught them. You said "I really don't know about that anything" and then what were your words following that phrase?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was not my job description. I wasn't involved in the workings of that so I didn't have any personal knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, in your answer you just said that you know what I was told by others, can you tell the Court what you heard about the intelligence or counter-intelligence support from other members of the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: That they were deployed in other agencies as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you give an example if you heard of any such example?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm really sorry to leap up. My learned friend appears to be reading from a document, none of this has been disclosed. We had no idea the witness was going to discuss the counter-intelligence support unit of this special unit. I'm not sure what notes my learned friend has, but they clearly have arisen from an interview with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I will skip this question and move ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, why do you think it was Frenki Simatovic in particular who made this speech to President Milosevic and the others at this award ceremony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my learned colleague is now asking the witness to speculate as to why something was done by my client. He is asking this witness to speculate. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, asking the witness to speculate, but I would agree that we need a factual foundation for any opinion because you are seeking an opinion. Is there anything known to you which would allow you to tell us why it was Mr. Simatovic in particular who made that speech? I'm not asking you to speculate on these matters, but whether there is anything to your knowledge what explains why it was Mr. Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, because he was the founder of the unit, the first person who founded this unit in 1991 when it was established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what's the basis for that knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the basis of this knowledge is that all the previous instructors who were there, who were there in 1995 and 1996, they said that he was the founder of the unit, as the concept itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you were told this and that you can't -- you have no other knowledge of fact why it was Mr. Simatovic which had to give that speech at that time? Mr. Hoffmann, I'm wondering what the question could tell us, but we want knowledge of facts rather than understanding of what others said or what would have been logical. You may put the next question to the witness. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, I just need to intervene in the transcript. Line 7 -- not everything that the witness said was translated. There was something else that the witness said in the Serbian language but that was not interpreted and that is not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Line 7 of page 77?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, page 77, between lines 4 to 7, so in that reply of the witness there was some additional information that was not interpreted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'll read to you what is found in those lines and could you please then tell us what you said in addition to what I read. "Well, the basis of this knowledge is that all the previous instructors who were there, who were there in 1995 and 1996, they said that he was the founder of the unit," and then it says, "as the concept itself." Could you tell us what you told us in addition to what I just read?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I said that he was not personally there in the territory but that he was the founder of the unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic, this meets your --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: We will continue to play clip 3. So it's the same clip still, and we go until 19 minutes 59.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, one of the things I'm wondering. You are supposed to -- not to lead this witness and there have been objections about it. First, to show what someone else told us and then to say is this what you know as well. Wouldn't it be appropriate to do it the other way around, to ask the witness anything you know already is on the video, and, of course, the witness for the sequences to follow is not aware. Then ask him what he knows about it and then look at it whether there's any need to play it again because then we know what the witness can tell us rather than that the witness gives his observations on whether it's consistent with what others told him because the answers are there already. So I would invite you to do it the other way around. Put questions in relation to what you know to be there and then to see what that brings us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Okay. The following parts of the clips are just basically footage, and I'm just going to ask the witness about what is shown on the footage. I think insofar that should cause no concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if it's not about -- if it is about who is there or could you locate that, if it's no further speeches, I have no problems, but if it would be further speeches to be confirmed as to the content by the witness, then I would oppose. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: We'll then play -- continue to play clip 3 and we'll play it until 19 minutes 59.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "What about these? They don't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, during the time that you were at Kula did you have occasion to be in the room shown on this video?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And who are the people whose pictures are appearing on the wall here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Members of the unit who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And can you tell us where the flags that can be seen at the bottom of the screen shot were coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Those were the flags that had been captured during combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: We will continue the same clip until 20 minutes 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell the Court what is on this plaque shown on this screen shot at 20 minutes 28?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: I believe that this is the unit's anthem. Yes, it is, the anthem of the special operations unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Did you ever personally receive such a plaque?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, I do have it somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: We continue with this clip until 20 minutes 46.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "These are the places where we ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, at this screen shot at 20 minutes 46, can you tell us what the item on the wall is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: It's a map depicting the places where the training camps were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: We then play clip 4 which starts at 22 minutes 12 seconds of the original tape and we pause again at 22 minutes 38.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Mr. President, dear guests, let us pay tribute to Deputy Minister Radovan Stojicic, Badza, by observing a minute of silence. Glory to him. Glory."

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, we've just heard Jovica Stanisic asking for a minute of silence to honour Radovan Stojicic aka Badza. Do you know who that person was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, I know he was a police general.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: We will then continue with clip 5, which starts at 40 minutes 44 seconds of the original tape and stop at 40 minutes 55.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "They are the best. They have reason to ... Good-bye."

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, just for the record, we look now at the time code 40 minutes 56. Who are the two men who just shook hands?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Franko Simatovic and Slobodan Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And we continue until 41 minute 10 seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Thank you, Radojica, all the best. Great heros."

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us who is now shaking hands with Milosevic if you can tell at 41 minutes, 10 seconds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: I see there Radojica Bozovic and Slobodan Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And we are still talking about the same and one Rajo Bozovic as before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, it is the same Rajo Bozovic who was at the Ozren camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Okay. We have one last short clip and that is clip 6. It starts at 43 minutes, 15 seconds, and we stop again at 43 minutes, 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell the Court what Jovica Stanisic is doing in this clip?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: He is greeting -- exchanging greetings with Captain Dragan.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And we continue until 43:51.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "I'm proud to present you with ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the person that Captain Dragan goes to after receiving the gift from Jovica Stanisic shown at 43 minutes, 51 seconds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Just for the record, can you tell the Court who he is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-005
utterances.text: Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, in light of the time, I would rather pause here before I move into a new area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if there's no area which you could cover within the next 6 minutes, then we'll have an early adjournment. Could you give us an indication as to how much time you'd still need. The Chamber is aware that in the beginning of today some additional time was take by matters of a procedural nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: There are maybe four or five documents that I want to show to the witness, and then about two clips of total 2 minutes with some additional questions on those clips. Depending on how far we go ahead with those documents, we'll have some basic questions, I think that could be done maybe in a half an hour tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you'd certainly finish within the first session, is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: That would certainly be my aim. And if I just maybe -- I don't know where the Defence stands at the moment, but it may be worth that if we meet outside the courtroom just to look at the four documents that I have at hand if we can expedite the discussion tomorrow in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Make your aim a reality, Mr. Hoffmann, I would say then. That's for at least the Chamber is expect you to do. I think the parties would need some guidance as to the start of the cross-examination. The Defence teams are invited that the request for postponing cross-examination as a whole is not granted. Therefore, the Defence teams are expected to cross-examine the witness and the Chamber will then see whether there will be any further request for more time for further preparations or for a recall of the witness once you have exhausted all the possibilities that are there, and the Chamber certainly in considering such a request will expect the party to show good cause why the matter which -- the matter on which the witness cannot be cross-examined on yet, why it was impossible to prepare for that issue. This may serve as guidance for the parties. I do not know whether any arrangement has been made as to who will start. You may have considered who is the first one not to start, but because that seems to be the common position of the Defence teams, but now you'll have to consider who will start the cross-examination. And the Chamber would then hear from you. Witness JF-005, we'll adjourn for the day and I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone or communicate in any other way with anyone about your testimony, whether that is testimony you've given today or testimony still to be given in the days to come. We will adjourn and we resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 21st of January, quarter past 2.00 in this same Courtroom II.
